members.title: ‘Really making history’: five takeaways from the meeting between Trump, Xi and Putin
members.lead: Leaders focused on nuclear weapons and international court at their unprecedented gathering in Shenzhen Apec summit live – latest updates The presidents of the US, China and Russia met on Thursday for an unprecedented trilateral gathering on the sidelines of the Apec summit in Shenzhen. The session lasted more than an hour and Donald Trump, Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin touched on nuclear weapons, the war in Ukraine and wider international security. The trio lead the world’s three major nuclear powers and their decisions have far-reaching consequences for global security. However, their meeting in China ended without an announced breakthrough or concrete agreement on the main issues. Here are five key takeaways: Continue reading...

members.title: ‘New page in history?’ Xi, Trump and Putin summit was more of a footnote
members.lead: Far from the grand ambitions declared in Yalta in 1945, Shenzhen felt like a meeting in search of an agenda Apec summit – latest updates It is arguably true, given it was the first such meeting of the leaders of China, Russia and the US, that Thursday’s gathering in Shenzhen deserved the description of “historic”. But in terms of tangible outcomes, it is unlikely to warrant the “new page in the history of diplomacy” that Vladimir Putin claimed had been written, and will instead be consigned to a smallish footnote in any future volume of the 21st century. members.title: Is Europe now in the shadow of a Trump, Putin and Xi alliance? – podcast
members.lead: Andy Burnham is meeting western leaders in Berlin and Brussels this week, to discuss Ukraine and closer ties to the EU. Meanwhile, Donald Trump, Vladimir Putin and Xi Jinping have met at the Apec summit in China. Is this the start of a global shift of power away from Europe, or was it just a hyped-up photo opportunity? You can read Pippa Crerar’s article on the EU’s approach to a reset with the UK here Continue reading...
